newsitem.title: USA: Tyson sees lower-than-forecast Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: Tyson sees lower-than-forecast Q3 profit.

text.p: Tyson Foods Inc said on Thursday that it does not expect to meet Wall Street's earnings forecasts for the third quarter because of operating and margin pressures.
Analysts on average had expected the poultry producer to earn $0.27 a share for the third quarter ending in late June, according to a First Call survey.
In last year's third quarter, Tyson reported earnings of $14.6 million, or $0.10 a share, on sales of $1.6 billion.

Tyson said margins were under pressure because of earlier disruptions in the company's Russian shipments and lower-than-expected prices overall, particularly for leg quarters and related dark meat products.
Tyson said its operating performance was similar to that of the second quarter ended March 1997, when it reported earnings of $48.2 million, or $0.22 a share.
Shipments of leg quarters to Russia are now moving at acceptable levels, but increased tariffs and other costs have hurt operations, Tyson said in a statement.
